topics.title: Prices weigh on voter mood
topics.summary: AP reported a new AP-NORC poll found many Americans still blame President Trump's policies for high prices, keeping everyday costs central as midterm campaigning intensifies.
topics.discussionPrompt: When prices become the whole kitchen-table conversation, who starts with policy and who just wants to compare grocery receipts?

topics.title: Campaigns chase midterm energy
topics.summary: AP said President Trump and Vice President JD Vance are campaigning in Republican-leaning areas as candidates try to build enthusiasm before November's midterm elections.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a campaign visits friendly territory, who calls it smart morale-building and who asks whether it changes any minds?

topics.title: Governors races carry big stakes
topics.summary: AP reported competitive governor races in several states could decide whether one party controls both legislative chambers and the governor's office, shaping state policy power.
topics.discussionPrompt: When state races decide who can actually pass things, who pays close attention and who admits they only know the national drama?

topics.title: Astronaut crew launches fast
topics.summary: AP reported SpaceX launched four astronauts toward the International Space Station on a quick trip, including a Canadian astronaut whose family has a baby due while he is away.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your work trip is orbit, who focuses on the science and who immediately worries about missing the family group chat?

topics.title: Energy permitting deal advances
topics.summary: AP reported senators from both parties reached a deal to speed approvals for energy and infrastructure projects as electricity demand grows and reviews often take years.
topics.discussionPrompt: If building power projects gets faster, who cheers the progress and who wants to double-check what protections stay in place?

topics.title: Cars raise privacy worries
topics.summary: The Guardian reported Dutch intelligence chiefs warned connected car technology could expose cameras, microphones and GPS data to hostile states, especially amid concerns over imported vehicles.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your car can collect that much data, who gets creeped out first and who starts hunting for the privacy settings?

topics.title: Male contraceptive research inches forward
topics.summary: The Guardian's Thursday briefing highlighted renewed attention on the long-running search for a male contraceptive pill, with researchers still working through science, safety and adoption questions.
topics.discussionPrompt: If contraception options finally became more balanced, who says about time and who wonders how people would actually split responsibility?

topics.title: Swiss glaciers shrink sharply
topics.summary: The Guardian reported Swiss glaciers have lost about 20% of their volume in five years, with scientists describing unusually rapid melt rates across the Alps.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a landscape changes that fast, who wants the science details and who thinks about the towns, trails and memories tied to it?

topics.title: Slackliner crosses Seoul skyline
topics.summary: The Guardian reported Estonian daredevil Jaan Roose completed a high slackline walk near Seoul's Gyeongbokgung palace, crossing a narrow ribbon 120 metres above the city.
topics.discussionPrompt: Watching someone balance above a city, who says beautiful, who says absolutely not, and who asks how the shoes work?

topics.title: U.S. may host club tournament
topics.summary: The Guardian reported the United States is lined up to host the first Women's Club World Cup, adding another major event to a fast-growing global women's soccer calendar.
topics.discussionPrompt: If clubs from around the world meet in one tournament, who picks a team by tactics and who picks by best kit colors?
